chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subbah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who sends money to a land, the one whom he wants to send it with says, 'Lend it to me, and I will pay you back when you arrive in the land.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give money to a traveler as a loan to be repaid later?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility of commercial law in Shia jurisprudence, permitting a traveler to convert entrusted funds into a personal loan (qard) with the obligation to repay upon arrival in the destination. It underscores the principle of mutual consent (taradi) in transforming the nature of a transaction from simple custody (amanah) to debt, reflecting the practical needs of trade in early Islamic societies. The ruling validates the validity of such arrangements provided the terms are clear, aligning with the broader Shia emphasis on facilitating lawful economic interactions.
